BIOMASS: ESA's forest mission¶

Objective: Analyze BIOMASS products, specially Level-1c Stack interferometric (STA) and Level-2a Forest Height (FH).

Introduction: BIOMASS Mission¶

Objective: Quantify forest carbon stocks and changes globally by measuring above-ground forest biomass and forest height (FH).

  • Overview - ESA Website
  • Documentation
  • IEEE Paper - BIOMASS: ESA’s P-Band SAR Mission

Setup & configuration¶

Credentials are read from .env (see README.md).

# --- Test site: bounding box and time range ---
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Site:
    """A validation test site (bbox = min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat)."""
    name: str
    bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float]
    start: str              # ISO date, inclusive
    end: str | None = None  # ISO date

    @property
    def datetime_range(self) -> str:
        """STAC/OGC datetime interval"""
        end = f"{self.end}T23:59:59Z" if self.end else ".."
        return f"{self.start}T00:00:00Z/{end}"

ESA MAAP catalogue via pystac-client¶

BIOMASS data is served from the ESA MAAP STAC API.

Authorization Flow implemented following the ESA Data Access Guide:

  1. Get the ESA MAAP Long Lasting Token ESA IAM Portal.
  2. Converting ESA MAAP Offline Token to get Short-lived Data Access Token
  3. Set Bearer Token in the "Authorization: Bearer {token}" HTTP header
In [2]:
import requests
from functools import lru_cache
from pystac_client import Client
from tqdm import tqdm

LUT_ASSET = "enclosure_nc" # LUT asset on on L1c STA items
FH_TIFF_ASSET = "enclosure_i_fh_tiff" # FH GeoTIFF asset key on L2a items

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def maap_catalog() -> Client:
    """Open (and cache) the ESA MAAP STAC catalogue client."""
    return Client.open(ESA_MAAP_STAC_URL.rstrip("/") + "/")


def maap_list_biomass():
    """BIOMASS collections on the catalogue, sorted by id."""
    return sorted((c for c in maap_catalog().get_collections()
                   if "biomass" in c.id.lower()), key=lambda c: c.id)


def maap_search_items(collection, bbox=None, datetime_range=None,
                      keep_asset=None, max_items=None):
    """STAC item search by bbox + datetime (pystac_client auto-pages).

    ``keep_asset`` optionally filters to items that carry that asset key.
    """
    search = maap_catalog().search(
        collections=[collection], bbox=list(bbox) if bbox else None,
        datetime=datetime_range, max_items=max_items, method="GET")
    items = list(search.items())
    return [it for it in items if keep_asset in it.assets] if keep_asset else items


# --- Authenticated asset download (ESA bearer token) --------------
_MAAP_SESSION = requests.Session()
_MAAP_TOKEN_CACHE: dict = {}

def maap_access_token() -> str:
    """Return a valid MAAP access token, exchanging the 90-day offline token."""
    if not ESA_MAAP_OFFLINE_TOKEN:
        raise RuntimeError("No MAAP credentials. Set ESA_MAAP_OFFLINE_TOKEN in "
                           ".env (portal.maap.eo.esa.int, via Earthdata Login).")
    if _MAAP_TOKEN_CACHE.get("expires_at", 0) - 30 > time.time():
        return _MAAP_TOKEN_CACHE["access_token"]
    r = _MAAP_SESSION.post(ESA_MAAP_TOKEN_URL, timeout=60, data={
        "client_id": ESA_MAAP_CLIENT_ID, "client_secret": ESA_MAAP_CLIENT_SECRET,
        "grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": ESA_MAAP_OFFLINE_TOKEN,
        "scope": "offline_access openid"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    tok = r.json()
    _MAAP_TOKEN_CACHE.update(access_token=tok["access_token"],
                             expires_at=time.time() + tok.get("expires_in", 300))
    return tok["access_token"]


def maap_download_asset(item, asset_key=FH_TIFF_ASSET, dest_dir=RAW_DIR) -> Path:
    """Stream one asset of an item to dest_dir (authenticated, atomic)."""
    if asset_key not in item.assets:
        raise KeyError(f"'{asset_key}' not in {item.id}; have {list(item.assets)}")
    href = item.assets[asset_key].href
    dest_dir = Path(dest_dir); dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = dest_dir / href.split("?")[0].split("/")[-1]
    if out.exists():
        return out
    part = out.with_name(out.name + ".part")
    with _MAAP_SESSION.get(href, stream=True, timeout=300,
                           headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {maap_access_token()}"}) as r:
        r.raise_for_status()
        total = int(r.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)) or None
        with open(part, "wb") as f, tqdm(total=total, unit="B", unit_scale=True,
                                         desc=out.name) as bar:
            for chunk in r.iter_content(1 << 20):
                f.write(chunk); bar.update(len(chunk))
    part.replace(out)
    return out

print("MAAP STAC client ready:", ESA_MAAP_STAC_URL)

MAAP STAC client ready: https://catalog.maap.eo.esa.int/catalogue

Level-1c stack primer: coherence & interferometric phase¶

L1c STA stacks contains the co-registered interferometric phase and, in its *_lut.nc annotation, the quantities the height retrieval rests on, already computed by BPS on the ~90 m LUT grid:

  • interferometry/interferogram — the interferogram, delivered already flattened (BPS removes the reference/flat-earth screen during coregistration), i.e. the height-bearing phase $\phi_{tomo}\propto k_z z$.
  • coregistration/flatteningPhaseScreen — the DEM synthetic interferogram $\phi_{flat}$ that was removed.
  • interferometry/coherence — $|\gamma|$; coregistration/waveNumbers — the vertical wavenumber $k_z$ (rad/m).
  • geometry/latitude,longitude — per-pixel WGS84 geolocation.

Each stack has one coregistration primary (no interferogram — a scene isn't interfered with itself) and several secondaries.

In [7]:
_FILL = -9999.0
_LUT_VARS = {
    "ifg": "interferometry/interferogram",
    "flat": "coregistration/flatteningPhaseScreen",
    "coh": "interferometry/coherence",
    "kz": "coregistration/waveNumbers",
    "lat": "geometry/latitude",
    "lon": "geometry/longitude",
}
_LUT_CACHE: dict = {}

def _wrap(a):
    """Wrap phase into (-pi, pi]."""
    return np.angle(np.exp(1j * a))

def _stack_key(item):
    """(stack, track, frame) identifying the tomographic aperture of a granule."""
    m = re.search(r"BIO_(S\d)_STA.*?(T\d{3})_(F\d{3})", item.id)
    return (m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)) if m else ("?", "?", "?")

def biomass_stacks(items):
    """Group L1c STA granules into apertures keyed (stack, track, frame), date-sorted."""
    groups: dict = {}
    for it in items:
        groups.setdefault(_stack_key(it), []).append(it)
    for g in groups.values():
        g.sort(key=lambda it: it.datetime)
    return dict(sorted(groups.items()))

def _read_lut(item):
    """Download (if needed), read and memoize the BPS LUT arrays of one granule (fill->NaN).

    A stack primary has no interferogram/coherence, so those keys are absent.
    """
    if item.id in _LUT_CACHE:
        return _LUT_CACHE[item.id]
    import h5py
    nc = maap_download_asset(item, LUT_ASSET, dest_dir=RAW_DIR / "bio_l1c")
    out = {}
    with h5py.File(nc, "r") as h5:
        for k, p in _LUT_VARS.items():
            if p in h5:
                a = h5[p][:]
                out[k] = np.where(a == _FILL, np.nan, a)
    _LUT_CACHE[item.id] = out
    return out

def is_primary(raw) -> bool:
    """True if a LUT dict is a stack primary (no interferogram/coherence)."""
    return "ifg" not in raw or "coh" not in raw

def biomass_interferogram(item, coh_min=0.2, decimate=3):
    """Read one granule's BPS LUT and return arrays needed to map its phase."""
    raw = _read_lut(item)
    if is_primary(raw):
        raise ValueError(f"{item.id} is a stack primary (no interferogram).")
    coh = np.clip(raw["coh"], 0, 1)
    s = (slice(None, None, max(1, decimate)),) * 2
    st, tr, fr = _stack_key(item)
    return {
        "ifg": _wrap(raw["ifg"])[s].astype("float32"),
        "screen": (raw["flat"] - np.nanmean(raw["flat"]))[s].astype("float32"),
        "coh": coh[s].astype("float32"), "kz": raw["kz"][s].astype("float32"),
        "mask": (coh > coh_min)[s],
        "lon": raw["lon"][s].astype("float32"), "lat": raw["lat"][s].astype("float32"),
        "meta": {"date": str(item.datetime.date()), "stack": st, "track": tr,
                 "frame": fr, "coh_median": float(np.nanmedian(coh)),
                 "kz_median": float(np.nanmedian(np.abs(raw["kz"])))},
    }

def biomass_stack_metrics(items):
    """Coherence + geometry for every granule of every stack over the site."""
    def _sensing(it):
        s = it.properties.get("start_datetime") or it.properties.get("datetime")
        e = it.properties.get("end_datetime") or s
        f = lambda t: str(t)[:19].replace("T", " ")
        return f(s), f(e)
    rows = []
    for (st, tr, fr), group in biomass_stacks(items).items():
        for it in group:
            raw = _read_lut(it)
            primary = is_primary(raw)
            coh = np.nan if primary else np.clip(raw["coh"], 0, 1)
            kz = float(np.nanmedian(np.abs(raw["kz"]))) if "kz" in raw else np.nan
            start, end = _sensing(it)
            rows.append({"stack": st, "track": tr, "frame": fr, "start": start,
                "end": end, "role": "primary" if primary else "secondary",
                "coh_median": np.nan if primary else round(float(np.nanmedian(coh)), 3),
                "coh_p90": np.nan if primary else round(float(np.nanpercentile(coh, 90)), 3),
                "kz_median": round(kz, 3) if kz == kz else np.nan,
                "amb_height_m": round(2*np.pi/kz, 1) if kz and kz > 1e-6 else np.nan})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

print("L1c stack primer helpers ready.")

L1c stack primer helpers ready.

biomass_stack_metrics reads every stack's LUT and reports, one row per acquisition, the interferometric geometry and quality that the forest-height retrieval rests on:

column meaning
coh_median median interferometric coherence $\lvert\gamma\rvert$ between the two passes (0 = fully decorrelated / phase is noise, 1 = perfectly correlated / clean phase). The single best predictor of retrieval quality.
coh_p90 90th-percentile coherence — the high-quality tail (stable / sparse-vegetation pixels). A large coh_p90 − coh_median gap means coherence is spatially patchy.
kz_median median vertical wavenumber $\lvert k_z\rvert$ (rad m⁻¹), the phase-to-height conversion $\phi = k_z\,z$. Set by the interferometric baseline; larger $\lvert k_z\rvert$ = finer height sensitivity but faster volume decorrelation.
amb_height_m height of ambiguity $h_{amb} = 2\pi / k_z$ (m): the height that spans one full $2\pi$ phase cycle. Canopy taller than $h_{amb}$ wraps and aliases.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

secondaries = [it for g in biomass_stacks(l1c_items).values() for it in g
               if not is_primary(_read_lut(it))]
best = max(secondaries, key=lambda it: biomass_interferogram(it)["meta"]["coh_median"])
d = biomass_interferogram(best)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5), constrained_layout=True)
for a, key, cmap, title in [
    (ax[0], "ifg", "twilight", r"Flattened interferogram $\phi_{tomo}$ (rad)"),
    (ax[1], "screen", "twilight", r"Flattening phase screen $\phi_{flat}$ (rad, mean-removed)"),
    (ax[2], "coh", "magma", r"Coherence $|\gamma|$")]:
    arr = np.where(d["mask"], d[key], np.nan) if key == "ifg" else d[key]
    sc = a.pcolormesh(d["lon"], d["lat"], arr, cmap=cmap, shading="auto")
    fig.colorbar(sc, ax=a, shrink=0.7); a.set_title(title)
    a.set_xlabel("Longitude"); a.set_ylabel("Latitude")
fig.suptitle(f"BIOMASS L1c STA — stack {d['meta']['stack']} "
             f"{d['meta']['date']} (median |γ|={d['meta']['coh_median']:.2f})")
fig.savefig(FIGURES_DIR / "part1_l1c_interferogram.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()

LiDAR references via earthaccess (GEDI L2A and AfriSAR LVIS)¶

The two independent height references, both discovered through earthaccess (docs), a NASA CMR API library, filtered to the same site bbox and a temporal window. Both are read into a common (lon, lat, rh98) GeoDataFrame so the §3 validation pipeline is identical regardless of reference.

  • AfriSAR LVIS L2 (AFLVIS2) — airborne LiDAR, 2016 Gabon campaign; dense, wall-to-wall, metre-accurate geolocation. ASCII .TXT tables. Mirrored on the AWS Open Data Registry (streams from S3 on AWS us-west-2).
  • GEDI L2A (GEDI02_A, V003) — spaceborne full-waveform LiDAR; sparse orbital sampling, per-shot quality flags, near-contemporaneous with BIOMASS. HDF5, one group per beam. rh98 = the 98th-percentile relative height.
In [ ]:
import geopandas as gpd
import earthaccess

# --- AfriSAR LVIS L2 (airborne): ASCII .TXT, one row per shot ---------------
_LVIS2_FALLBACK_COLUMNS = (
    "LFID SHOTNUMBER TIME GLON GLAT ZG HLON HLAT ZH TLON TLAT ZT "
    "RH10 RH15 RH20 RH25 RH30 RH35 RH40 RH45 RH50 RH55 RH60 RH65 RH70 RH75 "
    "RH80 RH85 RH90 RH95 RH96 RH97 RH98 RH99 RH100 "
    "AZIMUTH INCIDENTANGLE RANGE COMPLEXITY CHANNEL_L1B CHANNEL_ZG CHANNEL_RH"
).split()

def _lvis_columns(path):
    """LVIS2 column names from the last #-comment header line (falls back to spec)."""
    last = None
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            if not line.startswith("#"):
                break
            last = line
    names = last.lstrip("#").split() if last else _LVIS2_FALLBACK_COLUMNS
    return names if {"GLON", "GLAT", "RH98"}.issubset(names) else list(_LVIS2_FALLBACK_COLUMNS)

def read_lvis_l2(path, metric=None):
    """Read one LVIS L2 .TXT granule into a GeoDataFrame (EPSG:4326)."""
    metric = metric or HEIGHT_METRIC
    names = _lvis_columns(path); col = metric.upper()
    usecols = [c for c in ("GLON", "GLAT", "ZG", col) if c in names]
    if not {"GLON", "GLAT", col}.issubset(usecols):
        raise ValueError(f"{Path(path).name}: missing GLON/GLAT/{col}.")
    df = pd.read_csv(path, sep=r"\s+", comment="#", header=None, names=names, usecols=usecols)
    df = df.rename(columns={"GLON": "lon", "GLAT": "lat", "ZG": "zg", col: metric})
    df.loc[df["lon"] > 180, "lon"] -= 360
    return gpd.GeoDataFrame(df, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(df["lon"], df["lat"]), crs="EPSG:4326")

# --- GEDI L2A (spaceborne): HDF5, one group per beam, per-shot quality ------
_GEDI_REQUIRED = ("lat_lowestmode", "lon_lowestmode", "rh", "sensitivity", "degrade_flag")
_GEDI_QUALITY_FIELDS = ("quality_flag", "l2a_quality_flag_rel3", "l2a_quality_flag_rel2")

def _gedi_version(path):
    m = re.search(r"V(\d+)", Path(path).stem)
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else 0

def gedi_dedupe(paths, version=GEDI_L2A_VERSION):
    """One file per granule (track/orbit/frame), keeping the requested processing version."""
    want = int(re.sub(r"\D", "", str(version)))
    best = {}
    for p in sorted(map(Path, paths)):
        if _gedi_version(p) != want:
            continue
        best[tuple(p.stem.split("_")[2:5])] = p
    return sorted(best.values())

def read_gedi_l2a(path, metric=None):
    """Read one GEDI L2A HDF5 granule into a GeoDataFrame (ground location, rh<NN>, quality)."""
    import h5py
    metric = metric or HEIGHT_METRIC
    idx = int(re.sub(r"\D", "", metric))
    frames = []
    with h5py.File(path, "r") as h:
        for bname in (k for k in h.keys() if k.startswith("BEAM")):
            g = h[bname]
            qfield = next((n for n in _GEDI_QUALITY_FIELDS if n in g), None)
            if qfield is None or not all(n in g for n in _GEDI_REQUIRED) or g["rh"].shape[0] == 0:
                continue
            frames.append(pd.DataFrame({
                "lon": g["lon_lowestmode"][:], "lat": g["lat_lowestmode"][:],
                metric: g["rh"][:, idx].astype("float64"),
                "quality": g[qfield][:].astype("int8"), "degrade": g["degrade_flag"][:].astype("int16"),
                "sensitivity": g["sensitivity"][:].astype("float64")}))
    if not frames:
        raise ValueError(f"{Path(path).name}: no readable beams.")
    df = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    df.loc[df["lon"] > 180, "lon"] -= 360
    return gpd.GeoDataFrame(df, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(df["lon"], df["lat"]), crs="EPSG:4326")

# --- Shared read / curate / cache / staging ---------------------------------
def read_many_points(paths, reader, metric=None):
    """Read + concatenate several point granules with `reader` (skips unreadable files)."""
    metric = metric or HEIGHT_METRIC
    gdfs = []
    for p in paths:
        try:
            g = reader(p, metric=metric)
        except (ValueError, OSError, pd.errors.ParserError):
            continue
        if len(g):
            gdfs.append(g)
    if not gdfs:
        raise RuntimeError("No shots read — check granule paths / format.")
    return gpd.GeoDataFrame(pd.concat(gdfs, ignore_index=True), crs="EPSG:4326")

def curate_shots(gdf, bbox=None, metric=None, min_height=0.0, max_height=120.0,
                 min_sensitivity=None, require_quality=False):
    """Filter shots to a plausible canopy range + bbox; apply GEDI quality flags when present."""
    metric = metric or HEIGHT_METRIC
    keep = (gdf[metric] > min_height) & (gdf[metric] < max_height)
    if require_quality and "quality" in gdf:
        keep &= (gdf["quality"] == 1) & (gdf["degrade"] == 0)
    if min_sensitivity is not None and "sensitivity" in gdf:
        keep &= gdf["sensitivity"] > min_sensitivity
    out = gdf[keep]
    if bbox is not None:
        out = out.cx[bbox[0]:bbox[2], bbox[1]:bbox[3]]
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

# Per-reference spec: format reader + search params + curation (quality for GEDI only).
LIDAR = {
    "lvis": dict(short_name=AFRISAR_LVIS_SHORT_NAME, subdir="lvis", pattern="LVIS*.TXT",
                 temporal=AFRISAR_TEMPORAL, version=None, reader=read_lvis_l2,
                 dedupe=sorted, curate={}),
    "gedi": dict(short_name=GEDI_L2A_SHORT_NAME, subdir="gedi", pattern="GEDI02_A_*.h5",
                 temporal=GEDI_TEMPORAL, version=GEDI_L2A_VERSION, reader=read_gedi_l2a,
                 dedupe=gedi_dedupe, curate=dict(min_sensitivity=0.9, require_quality=True)),
}

def curated_cache_path(kind, site=None):
    """Path of the cached curated-shots table (raw granules can be deleted afterwards)."""
    return INTERIM_DIR / f"{kind}_shots_qc_{(site or SITE).name}.pkl"

def local_granules(kind):
    """Downloaded granules for a reference under data/raw/<subdir> (GEDI version-deduped)."""
    spec = LIDAR[kind]
    return spec["dedupe"]((RAW_DIR / spec["subdir"]).glob(spec["pattern"]))

def stage_lidar(kind, site=None):
    """Curated shots for one reference: cache -> local raw granules -> Earthdata download."""
    site = site or SITE
    spec = LIDAR[kind]
    cache = curated_cache_path(kind, site)
    if cache.exists():
        df = pd.read_pickle(cache)
        return gpd.GeoDataFrame(df, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(df["lon"], df["lat"]), crs="EPSG:4326")
    paths = local_granules(kind)
    if not paths:                                    # nothing local -> fetch from Earthdata
        earthaccess.login(persist=True)
        results = earthaccess.search_data(short_name=spec["short_name"], bounding_box=site.bbox,
            temporal=spec["temporal"], **({"version": spec["version"]} if spec["version"] else {}))
        if not results:
            raise RuntimeError(f"No {spec['short_name']} granules over '{site.name}'.")
        dest = RAW_DIR / spec["subdir"]; dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        paths = spec["dedupe"](Path(f) for f in earthaccess.download(results, str(dest)))
    shots = curate_shots(read_many_points(paths, spec["reader"]), bbox=site.bbox, **spec["curate"])
    pd.DataFrame(shots.drop(columns="geometry")).to_pickle(cache)
    return shots

print("LiDAR helpers ready (LVIS + GEDI).")

Stage the LiDAR references¶

GEDI .h5 files are multi-GB per orbit but the curated shot tables are tiny, so we cache them to a pickle (.pkl) - after the first build you can delete data/raw/{gedi,lvis} and the notebook still reloads instantly.

In [11]:
def staged(kind):
    """Stage a reference if its cache/local granules exist or downloading is enabled, else None."""
    if curated_cache_path(kind).exists() or local_granules(kind):
        return stage_lidar(kind)
    return None

lvis_shots, gedi_shots = staged("lvis"), staged("gedi")
for name, shots in [("LVIS", lvis_shots), ("GEDI", gedi_shots)]:
    print(f"{name} curated shots: {len(shots):,}")

Validation¶

Validate ESA's official L2a Forest Height product against two independent LiDAR benchmark references (AfriSAR LVIS airborne and GEDI L2A spaceborne).

  1. AfriSAR LVIS airborne LiDAR — dense, wall-to-wall canopy-height truth. EarthData
  2. GEDI L2A spaceborne LiDAR — sparse but near-contemporaneous cross-check. EarthData

For each reference we co-register the point cloud to the FH grid with rioxarray and quantify accuracy with RMSE, bias, R² plus scatter, residual maps, and an error-by-height-class breakdown that exposes saturation.

In [12]:
import rasterio
import rioxarray  # registers the .rio accessor
import xarray as xr
from rasterio.merge import merge as _rio_merge
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score


# ---- Raster mosaic / IO -----------------------------------------------------
def build_fh_mosaic(raster_paths, dest=None) -> Path:
    """Mosaic FH tiles into one GeoTIFF by per-pixel median over overlaps.

    The tiles are repeat / cross-orbit passes of the same forest, and some are
    low-coherence retrievals whose forest height has collapsed toward the ground.
    An order-independent per-pixel *median* is robust to those outlier passes,
    where a plain mean would blend them in. NoData is ignored per pixel.
    """
    paths = [str(p) for p in raster_paths]
    if not paths:
        raise ValueError("No FH tiles given to mosaic.")
    dest = Path(dest) if dest else (INTERIM_DIR / "fh_mosaic.tif")
    # Common target grid = union of all tiles (rasterio.merge computes its extent).
    merged, transform = _rio_merge(paths, nodata=-9999.0)
    h, w = merged.shape[1], merged.shape[2]
    tiles = [load_raster(p) for p in paths]  # masked DataArrays, NoData -> NaN
    grid = tiles[0].rio.reproject(tiles[0].rio.crs, transform=transform, shape=(h, w))
    stack = np.stack([t.rio.reproject_match(grid).values for t in tiles])
    med = np.nanmedian(stack, axis=0)
    band = np.where(np.isfinite(med), med, -9999.0).astype("float32")
    with rasterio.open(paths[0]) as s0:
        meta = s0.meta.copy()
    meta.update(height=h, width=w, transform=transform, count=1,
                dtype="float32", nodata=-9999.0)
    with rasterio.open(dest, "w", **meta) as dst:
        dst.write(band, 1)
    return dest


def load_raster(path) -> xr.DataArray:
    """Open a single-band raster as a masked DataArray (NoData -> NaN)."""
    da = rioxarray.open_rasterio(path, masked=True)
    return da.squeeze("band", drop=True) if da.sizes.get("band") == 1 else da


# ---- Co-register LiDAR footprints to the FH grid ----------------------------
def sample_fh_at_shots(fh_path, shots, out_col="biomass_fh"):
    """Sample FH at every LiDAR shot, tagging each with its value and pixel (row, col).

    One ``rasterio`` pass; points are reprojected to the raster CRS, NoData -> NaN.
    """
    with rasterio.open(fh_path) as src:
        pts = shots.to_crs(src.crs)
        xs, ys = pts.geometry.x.to_numpy(), pts.geometry.y.to_numpy()
        fh = np.array([v[0] for v in src.sample(np.column_stack([xs, ys]))], "float64")
        if src.nodata is not None:
            fh[fh == src.nodata] = np.nan
        rows, cols = rasterio.transform.rowcol(src.transform, xs, ys)
    out = shots.copy()
    out[out_col] = fh
    out["_row"], out["_col"] = np.asarray(rows), np.asarray(cols)
    return out


def pixel_means(sampled, ref_col, out_col="biomass_fh"):
    """Average LiDAR footprints (and their FH pixel) within each FH pixel."""
    d = sampled.dropna(subset=[ref_col, out_col])
    return (d.groupby(["_row", "_col"], as_index=False)
             .agg(**{f"{ref_col}_pixmean": (ref_col, "mean"), out_col: (out_col, "mean")}))

print("Co-registration helpers ready.")

Co-registration helpers ready.
In [13]:
# ---- Metrics + figures ------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass
class Metrics:
    n: int; rmse: float; bias: float; mae: float; r2: float; pearson_r: float
    def as_dict(self): return asdict(self)
    def __str__(self):
        return (f"n={self.n}  RMSE={self.rmse:.2f} m  bias={self.bias:+.2f} m  "
                f"MAE={self.mae:.2f} m  R²={self.r2:.3f}  r={self.pearson_r:.3f}")

def compute_metrics(df, ref_col, pred_col) -> Metrics:
    """RMSE / bias / MAE / R² / Pearson r between a reference and predicted column."""
    d = df[[ref_col, pred_col]].dropna()
    ref = d[ref_col].to_numpy("float64"); pred = d[pred_col].to_numpy("float64")
    if len(ref) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Need >=2 paired samples, got {len(ref)}.")
    err = pred - ref
    return Metrics(len(ref), float(np.sqrt(np.mean(err**2))), float(np.mean(err)),
                   float(np.mean(np.abs(err))), float(r2_score(ref, pred)),
                   float(np.corrcoef(ref, pred)[0, 1]))

def metrics_by_class(df, ref_col, pred_col, bins=(0, 15, 25, 35, 45, 120)):
    """Bias + RMSE per reference-height class (exposes saturation)."""
    d = df[[ref_col, pred_col]].dropna()
    ref = d[ref_col].to_numpy("float64"); pred = d[pred_col].to_numpy("float64")
    err = pred - ref; rows = []
    for lo, hi in zip(bins[:-1], bins[1:]):
        m = (ref >= lo) & (ref < hi)
        if not m.any():
            continue
        e = err[m]
        rows.append({"class": f"{lo:g}-{hi:g} m", "n": int(m.sum()),
                     "mean_ref": float(ref[m].mean()), "mean_pred": float(pred[m].mean()),
                     "bias": float(e.mean()), "rmse": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(e**2)))})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def scatter_plot(df, ref_col, pred_col, metrics=None,
                 ref_label="LiDAR RH98 (m)", pred_label="BIOMASS Forest Height (m)",
                 title="BIOMASS Forest Height vs LiDAR", save_as=None, max_plot_points=50000):
    """1:1 scatter with identity line, least-squares fit, and a metrics box."""
    d = df[[ref_col, pred_col]].dropna()
    metrics = metrics or compute_metrics(d, ref_col, pred_col)
    lim = float(np.nanmax([d[ref_col].max(), d[pred_col].max()])) * 1.05
    dplot = d.sample(max_plot_points, random_state=0) if len(d) > max_plot_points else d
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
    ax.scatter(dplot[ref_col], dplot[pred_col], s=8, alpha=0.35, edgecolor="none")
    ax.plot([0, lim], [0, lim], "k--", lw=1, label="1:1")
    b1, b0 = np.polyfit(d[ref_col], d[pred_col], 1)
    xs = np.linspace(0, lim, 100)
    ax.plot(xs, b1*xs + b0, "r-", lw=1.2, label=f"fit: y={b1:.2f}x+{b0:.1f}")
    ax.set_xlim(0, lim); ax.set_ylim(0, lim)
    ax.set_xlabel(ref_label); ax.set_ylabel(pred_label); ax.set_title(title)
    ax.text(0.03, 0.97, str(metrics), transform=ax.transAxes, va="top", ha="left",
            fontsize=8, bbox=dict(boxstyle="round", fc="white", alpha=0.8))
    ax.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=8); ax.set_aspect("equal"); fig.tight_layout()
    if save_as:
        fig.savefig(save_as, dpi=150)
    return fig, ax

def residual_map(gdf, ref_col, pred_col, title="Residuals (FH − LiDAR)",
                 save_as=None, max_plot_points=80000):
    """Map of per-point residuals, diverging scale centred at zero."""
    d = gdf.dropna(subset=[ref_col, pred_col]).copy()
    d["residual"] = d[pred_col] - d[ref_col]
    vmax = float(np.nanpercentile(np.abs(d["residual"]), 95)) or 1.0
    if len(d) > max_plot_points:
        d = d.sample(max_plot_points, random_state=0)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
    sc = ax.scatter(d.geometry.x, d.geometry.y, c=d["residual"], cmap="RdBu_r",
                    vmin=-vmax, vmax=vmax, s=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("Longitude"); ax.set_ylabel("Latitude"); ax.set_title(title)
    fig.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, label="Residual (m)"); fig.tight_layout()
    if save_as:
        fig.savefig(save_as, dpi=150)
    return fig, ax

def save_report_row(metrics, label, path=None) -> Path:
    """Upsert a metrics row into the report CSV (idempotent on the label)."""
    path = path or (PROCESSED_DIR / "validation_summary.csv")
    row = {"comparison": label, **metrics.as_dict()}
    if path.exists():
        df = pd.read_csv(path)
        match = df.index[df["comparison"] == label]
        if len(match):
            for col, val in row.items():
                df.loc[match[0], col] = val
        else:
            df = pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame([row])], ignore_index=True)
    else:
        df = pd.DataFrame([row])
    df.to_csv(path, index=False)
    return path

print("Metrics + figure helpers ready.")

L2A_DIR = RAW_DIR / "bio_l2a"
FH_MOSAIC = INTERIM_DIR / "fh_mosaic.tif"

def reference_fh_mosaic():
    """Path to the site's L2a FH mosaic: reuse the cache, else mosaic the local tiles,
    else download the discovered tiles from MAAP (needs a token). None if unavailable."""
    if FH_MOSAIC.exists():
        return FH_MOSAIC
    tiles = sorted(L2A_DIR.glob("bio_fp_fh__l2a_*_fh.tiff"))
    if not tiles and fh_items and ESA_MAAP_OFFLINE_TOKEN:
        tiles = [maap_download_asset(it, FH_TIFF_ASSET, dest_dir=L2A_DIR) for it in fh_items]
    return build_fh_mosaic(tiles, dest=FH_MOSAIC) if tiles else None

Benchmark against LiDAR (AfriSAR LVIS + GEDI L2A)¶

One routine, run for each reference. It samples the FH product at every LiDAR footprint (rasterio) and reports two supports: the raw footprint comparison (each shot vs the pixel it falls in, used for the residual map) and a pixel-mean match (LiDAR footprints averaged within each FH pixel - the fairest like-for-like and the number to quote), plus an error-by-height-class table that reveals saturation.

In [16]:
def validate_against_lidar(fh_raster, shots, label, ref_label):
    """FH-vs-LiDAR validation at two supports: raw footprint and pixel-mean."""
    if fh_raster is None or shots is None or not len(shots):
        print(f"[{label}] skipped - need an FH raster and curated {label} shots.")
        return None
    metric = HEIGHT_METRIC
    sampled = sample_fh_at_shots(fh_raster, shots)

    # Footprint support: each LiDAR shot vs the FH pixel it falls in (residual map).
    fp = sampled.dropna(subset=[metric, "biomass_fh"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    m_fp = compute_metrics(fp, ref_col=metric, pred_col="biomass_fh")
    save_report_row(m_fp, f"L2A_FH_vs_{label}_footprint")

    # Pixel-mean support: LiDAR footprints averaged within each FH pixel (fairest).
    agg = pixel_means(sampled, ref_col=metric)
    m_pix = compute_metrics(agg, ref_col=f"{metric}_pixmean", pred_col="biomass_fh")
    save_report_row(m_pix, f"L2A_FH_vs_{label}_pixelmean")

    print(f"[{label}] footprint  : {m_fp}")
    print(f"[{label}] pixel-mean : {m_pix}")

    scatter_plot(agg, ref_col=f"{metric}_pixmean", pred_col="biomass_fh", metrics=m_pix,
                 ref_label=f"{ref_label} RH98 (m)", title=f"BIOMASS FH vs {ref_label}",
                 save_as=FIGURES_DIR / f"part2_{label.lower()}_scatter.png")
    plt.show()
    residual_map(fp, ref_col=metric, pred_col="biomass_fh",
                 title=f"Residuals (FH - {ref_label} RH98)",
                 save_as=FIGURES_DIR / f"part2_{label.lower()}_residual.png")
    plt.show()
    by_class = metrics_by_class(agg, ref_col=f"{metric}_pixmean", pred_col="biomass_fh")
    print(f"[{label}] error by height class:")
    display(by_class)
    return {"footprint": m_fp, "pixelmean": m_pix, "by_class": by_class}

BPS: Data Processing¶

The BIOMASS Processing Suite (BPS) is the collection of operational processors for BIOMASS mission, in charge of processing BIOMASS Level-0 data up to Level-3, generating a wide set of products.

The chain¶

L1c STA stacks ─▶ bps_l2a_processor ─▶ BIO_FP_FH__L2A   (per-stack Forest Height)
  (+ aux: PP2 config,   │  FH  = PolInSAR / RVoG inversion
   FNF mask, DEM)       │  TFH = TomoSAR (tomographic FH)
                        └─▶ also FD (disturbance), GN (ground notch)
BIO_FP_FH__L2A (all stacks) ─▶ bps_l2b_fh_processor ─▶ BIO_FP_FH__L2B  (mosaic)

Forest Height is a Level-2a product (BIO_FP_FH__L2A) computed by bps-l2a_processor starting from a full L1c stack, including:

  • fh/ sub-processor implements the interferometric (PolInSAR) retrieval
  • tomo_fh/ sub-processor implements tomographic (TomoSAR) retrievel

bps-l2b_fh_processor aggregates all products covering the same location on the ground, generating a single BIOMASS L2b product tile.

Each processor is an ESA-style operational executable driven by a single JobOrder.xml that declares its inputs, auxiliary products and outputs.

Please refer to BIOMASS Documentation to deep dive into the documentation of each level, including ATBD (Algorithms Theoretical Baseline Document).

Interpretation¶

Against the LiDAR benchmarks, BIOMASS L2a Forest Height behaves as a saturating estimator: bias near zero on average but a fit slope well below 1, reading too tall over short canopy and too short over the tallest, accurate only in the mid-range it collapses toward (the error-by-class tables above make this explicit). LVIS (dense, wall-to-wall) is the primary quantitative benchmark; GEDI (sparse, near-contemporaneous) is an independent cross-check that also removes LVIS's ~10-year temporal offset.

Toward carbon (future work). Once ESA BIOMASS Above-Ground Biomass (AGB) products ship (expected ~2027), the same validated height pipeline feeds the fixed CO2e = AGB × 0.47 × 3.67 conversion (IPCC carbon fraction 0.47, CO₂/C mass ratio 3.67) to turn the map into tons of CO₂-equivalent.
